Definition: probably to look askant, i.e. (figuratively) be jealous
BiblicalUsage: Ratsad is, probably, to look askant — to be jealous, to eye with envy. The psalm asks the high hills, 'Why leap ye, ye high hills? this is the hill which God desireth to dwell in; yea, the LORD will dwell in it for ever.'
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the leaping hills are envy in the landscape: the great mountains eye Zion with jealousy, and God chooses the little hill anyway.
